say.en: Turn a battery around in a circuit with a diode and the bulb goes out. A diode lets current flow one way and almost blocks it the other way. In this lesson: Draw the diode symbol and identify anode and cathode.
Explain forward and reverse bias.
Draw and explain the V-I characteristic with knee voltage and breakdown.

body.en: A p-n junction diode has two terminals: the anode (p-side) and the cathode (n-side); the arrow of its symbol points in the direction of conventional current. In forward bias (p to +, n to −) the applied voltage opposes the barrier potential, the depletion layer narrows and a large current flows once the voltage exceeds the cut-in voltage. In *reverse bias* (p to −, n to +) the depletion layer widens and only a tiny reverse saturation current I₀ of minority carriers flows.

points.en: *Forward*: p to +, large current after cut-in

narration.en: In forward bias the p-side goes to positive, the barrier is reduced, and a large current flows. In reverse bias the barrier grows and only a tiny current flows.

title.en: Forward bias, reverse bias and the V–I curve

say.en: Forward bias: the p-side, the anode, goes to the positive terminal. The battery opposes the barrier, so a large current flows.
On the graph, almost no current flows until about 0.7 volt for silicon. Then the current rises steeply. That voltage is the knee or cut-in voltage.
Reverse bias: the p-side goes to the negative terminal. The depletion layer widens and only a tiny current of minority carriers flows.
The diode equation ties it together: I equals I nought times e to the V by eta V T, minus one.

body.en: The forward curve stays near zero up to the knee (cut-in) voltage and then rises steeply. The reverse curve shows a small, nearly constant reverse saturation current, which doubles for about every 10 °C rise in temperature. At a large reverse voltage, the breakdown voltage, the reverse current rises suddenly. The curve follows the *diode* equation $I = I_0(e^{V/\eta V_T} - 1)$, with $V_T = kT/e \approx 26$ mV at room temperature and η = 1 for Ge, about 2 for Si.

steps.en: e^11.54 ≈ 1.03 × 10⁵, which is much larger than 1.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A silicon diode has I₀ = 10 nA and η = 2. Find the current at a forward voltage of 0.6 V at room temperature (V_T = 26 mV).

say.en: Let us solve this together. A silicon diode has I 0 equals 10 nA and eta equals 2. Find the current at a forward voltage of 0.6 volts at room temperature V T equals 26 mV.
eta V T equals 2 times 0.026 equals 0.052 volts, so V/ eta V T equals 0.6 over 0.052 is approximately 11.54.
e^11.54 is approximately 1.03 times 10 to the power 5, which is much larger than 1.
I is approximately 10 times 10 to the power minus 9 times 1.03 times 10 to the power 5 is approximately 1.03 times 10 to the power minus 3 A.
So the answer is I is approximately 1.0 milliampere.

problem.en: A diode has I₀ = 10 nA at 25 °C. Estimate I₀ at 55 °C.

steps.en: The rise is 55 − 25 = 30 °C, which is three steps of 10 °C.
I₀ doubles for each step: 10 × 2³ = 80 nA.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A diode has I₀ = 10 nA at 25 °C. Estimate I₀ at 55 °C.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A diode has I 0 equals 10 nA at 25 degrees Celsius. Estimate I 0 at 55 degrees Celsius.
The rise is 55 minus 25 equals 30 degrees Celsius, which is three steps of 10 degrees Celsius.
I 0 doubles for each step: 10 times 2 cubed equals 80 nA.
So the answer is I 0 is approximately 80 nA.

say.kn: ಕಟ್-ಇನ್ ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್:? Si 0.7 volts, Ge 0.3 volts; ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಹಿಮ್ಮುಖ ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಗಿತ.

say.en: Diode equation:? I equals I 0(e^(V/ eta V T) minus 1).
say.kn: ಡಯೋಡ್ ಸಮೀಕರಣ:? I equals I 0(e^(V/ eta V T) minus 1).

say.en: Next: Diode resistance, ratings and the ideal diode.
say.kn: ಮುಂದೆ: ಡಯೋಡ್ ರೋಧ, ರೇಟಿಂಗ್‌ಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಆದರ್ಶ ಡಯೋಡ್.
